data.body:
## S0 CLOSED; 2594 exonerated; the e2e defect is repo-wide at ~46% CI failure

S0 (7dfa) CLOSED on the third attempt, unblocking S6 (09da, bounded gate admission) and S1 (aa40,
dedicated EBS volume). ADR 0112 is on main at 85ef5ad33ada.

STALE-CODE QUESTION ANSWERED EMPIRICALLY, as I said I would rather than assume: the close SUCCEEDED
while review-plan --status still reported stale-code for the three file_impact paths. So an
attestation going stale because the ticket's OWN work landed does not block the close. Only
stale-MATERIAL (a description text edit) does. Good design; worth knowing.

2594 IS EXONERATED, AND MY EARLIER FRAMING WAS WRONG. I justified a recheck by calling the e2e
failure an 'intermittent race'. It is not intermittent. It is a FIXED, UNBOUNDED-COST fixture
against a FIXED budget whose cost has grown until it straddles the 300s cliff. Setup times for
test_emitted_bpmn_has_no_illegal_ids on jobs that PASSED: 40.96s, 101.86s, 201.58s, 271.35s -- the
last being 90% of budget. Over 300s, timeout_method='thread' calls os._exit(1) and kills the worker.
So WHICH matrix cells fail varies run to run while the cost does not, which is precisely why a
recheck could not clear it. That the recheck failed on two DIFFERENT Python versions was the tell,
and I should have treated it as disconfirming evidence immediately rather than as bad luck.

Three independent proofs 2594 did not cause it: (1) the failure predates 2594 reaching CI by ~20
minutes -- first occurrence run 33813339060 at 22:30:05Z against change 2592, while 2594 was
committed 22:50Z; (2) failing runs in one 30-minute window checked out four different changes
(2602, 2592, 2595, 2601); (3) no code path -- test_editor_e2e imports only rebar.llm.workflow.*, grep
for 'composer' across tests/e2e/ and src/rebar/llm/workflow/ returns nothing, and the _seam.py edit
is purely additive with zero deletions so string-named imports are unaffected. Stale base was also
checked and ruled out: 2594 is 5 commits behind, but none of the 33 files touched are under
tests/e2e/, .github/workflows/, pyproject.toml or tests/conftest.py.

SCALE: this defect is failing ~46% of ALL CI runs repo-wide -- 23 of 50 completed Verified runs
between 09-03 14:27Z and 09-04 03:01Z. Sharp onset: last clean run 22:02:43Z, first crash 22:30:05Z,
zero occurrences in the preceding 21 hours. It blocks every open change, so 9a17 is now priority 0
and change 2600 is the unblocker for the whole repository.

Two constraints fed to the 2600 agent that were not in the original ticket:
 - PLAYWRIGHT dominates the cold install and bpmn_harness does not need it (it is browser_runner's
   dependency). Excluding it from that provisioning path is the cheapest single lever.
 - The Verified lane runs workflows from TRUSTED MAIN, so a CI-side pre-provision step cannot be
   validated on the patchset that introduces it -- it only takes effect once merged. A still-red
   Verified on 2600 must not be misread as the CI step being wrong. That makes the PORTABLE
   in-process half the part that has to be right on the patchset, which is also what
   project.portability requires.
Also noted: macOS never exercises this at all -- DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS restricts that job to
platform_compat -- so the matrix hides the defect on one of four cells.

Posted the correction to Gerrit 2594 with the evidence and explicitly did NOT recheck: CONTRIBUTING
reserves recheck for a provably environmental fault, and this is a reproducible in-repo timing defect
with a measured mechanism.

S6 dispatched. S1 deliberately HELD: with CI failing ~46% repo-wide, adding changes to a broken gate
burns ~19 minutes of runner time per attempt and produces noise rather than signal. Landing 2600
first is the higher-value move.
